question: As the operator who locked confirm-then-burn and the §8 offline policy, I want to rule which behavior applies when a campaign's requires_online flag is not client-readable (tonight: no campaigns replica exists and the codes replica lacks the flag), so that the offline window stays usable without silently deleting the requires_online=true refusal. Raised by Card 6's G6 adversarial review (run 20260905, park-class ruling): the card built the §8 refusal fully — machine-guarded and e2e-pinned via an injectable policy seam — and defaulted unknown→false, i.e. the force-submit override is available behind the marketing-offline-override entitlement plus the §13 confirmation, with every such attempt audit-flagged offline_override=true. Consequence on tonight's real data: the refusal cannot fire on any code, because every campaign resolves to policy-unknown.
proposal: Ratify unknown→false as shipped (audit-flagged, entitlement-gated, revertible by one constant), plus a named follow-up card that replicates requires_online to devices and arms the refusal on real data BEFORE any real campaign is provisioned; Card 6 stays parked tonight — complete, all gates green, unmerged — until the operator answers.

votes.note: the §8 refusal is the close bar's offline-safety leg and this default makes every campaign overridable until the flag replicates — a product-policy call only the operator can settle; exposure tonight is zero (no live campaigns, no hosted substrate), but ratification must precede any real campaign
the card is complete and its gates are green; parking costs one morning decision, while merging would put an unreviewed policy default onto dev

unknown→true would kill the entire offline path (a dead product surface); unknown→false is entitlement-gated, audit-flagged, and cheaply revertible; the refusal mechanism itself is built and pinned wherever the flag IS known

weighing: No adopted delegation covers a §8 policy fork; P-1's bound excludes it explicitly and the signed slate's hard park note names it. The engineering is sound and expected to survive ratification unchanged, but the decision of record belongs to the operator.
reasons: top-severity questions are the operator's — no number of citations clears them
